title: Portability: wire the daemon importer dependency edge
description: Objective: land only the workspace dependency edge required for the daemon shadow reader, without mixing manifest/lock changes into its four-file production slice. Declare @moe/import for apps/daemon, refresh the importer lock entry, and prove the public bare specifier resolves from compiled daemon code.
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/package.json declares @moe/import as a workspace dependency and pnpm-lock.yaml contains the matching apps/daemon importer link to packages/import.

A temporary TypeScript probe located inside apps/daemon imports the required ShadowProjection types, decoder, and compareShadowProjections from the public bare @moe/import specifier and typechecks exit 0; the probe is deleted in the same command.
A negative control using a nonexistent bare specifier fails typecheck, proving the positive probe did not pass vacuously, and the normal daemon typecheck remains exit 0.
A plain-Node compiled import from the daemon package context resolves @moe/import without tsconfig paths, deep relative imports, or source-loader flags.
Only the two manifest/lock paths are committed, and no production call site or generated probe/scratch file remains; task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8 is recorded as the immediate consumer.
taskRails: Public package root only; no tsconfig paths, TypeScript project references, deep imports, root package workaround, or dependency reversal.
Run pnpm install only as needed to update the workspace lock importer; preserve unrelated lockfile/worktree changes and commit explicit owned paths.
The verification output must prove the @moe/daemon filter matched and executed; exit 0 with no compiler/test output is not evidence.
Do not implement the reader or edit @moe/import production sources in this task.

implementationPlan.description: Record the BEFORE state, so every later claim has a baseline to be measured against. Run and capture verbatim: (a) `node -e "const d=require('./apps/daemon/package.json').dependencies; console.log('@moe/import' in d)"` — expect `false`; (b) `grep -n "@moe/import" pnpm-lock.yaml` and note that `packages/import: {}` appears at :153 with NO dependents anywhere, so this task lands the FIRST edge into that package; (c) a compiled bare-specifier probe that must FAIL right now — write `apps/daemon/src/__import-edge-probe.ts` importing `compareShadowProjections` and `projectLegacyImport` plus the types `LegacyImportFacts`, `ShadowComparison` and `ShadowProjection` from the bare specifier `@moe/import`, run `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, capture the error, and DELETE the probe in the same command. Expect TS2307 "Cannot find module '@moe/import'" or the TS6059 rooted-directory error the undeclared-workspace-dep family produces. A probe that unexpectedly PASSES here means the edge already exists by some route and the whole task premise is wrong — stop and report rather than proceeding. Those five symbols are all confirmed present on the root barrel (index.ts:104-115) at plan time.

implementationPlan.description: Prove the edge with a compiled probe AND its negative control, which is the half that stops a vacuous pass. Recreate the same probe from step 1 at `apps/daemon/src/__import-edge-probe.ts`, run `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, and require exit 0 with NO diagnostic naming the probe file. Then, in the same run, the NEGATIVE CONTROL that DoD 3 demands: a second probe importing from a bare specifier that certainly does not exist (for example `@moe/does-not-exist`) MUST fail typecheck, and the failure must be a module-resolution error — read the actual code, because a probe that fails on a syntax error or an unused-variable rule would satisfy "it failed" while proving nothing about resolution. DELETE BOTH probes in the same command that creates them, and confirm afterwards with `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` that neither survives; rail 5 and the epic rail both forbid a probe or scratch file remaining. Finally re-run the plain `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and require it still exits 0.

implementationPlan.description: Prove RUNTIME resolution, not just types — DoD 4 is a separate claim from DoD 2 and a passing typecheck does not establish it. `@moe/import`'s manifest maps `exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}` — a `.ts` file — and this repo runs TypeScript directly under Node (apps/daemon's own `start` script is `node ./src/daemon-main.ts`), on Node v24.16.0 where type stripping is native and needs no flag. So the correct probe is a plain `node --input-type=module -e "import('@moe/import').then(m => console.log(typeof m.compareShadowProjections))"` executed with the working directory inside `apps/daemon`, printing `function`. NO tsconfig paths, NO deep relative import, NO loader or `--experimental-*` flag — if any of those is needed, the edge is not really landed and the task must report rather than paper over it. Run this from PowerShell, not the Bash tool: a prior plain-Node smoke on this repo failed only because Git Bash rewrote paths. Do NOT copy the precedent in `tools/import/import-shadow.ts`, which imports `../../packages/import/src/index.js` by deep relative path — that works only because `tools/` has no manifest of its own, and rail 1 forbids it here.
implementationPlan.note:
RUNTIME RESOLUTION PROVEN SEPARATELY FROM TYPES, WITH TWO CONTROLS. All from PowerShell, never the Bash tool, per the known Git-Bash path-rewriting hazard.

POSITIVE, cwd inside apps/daemon:
  node --input-type=module -e "import('@moe/import').then(m => console.log(typeof m.compareShadowProjections, typeof m.projectLegacyImport))"
  -> `RESOLVED typeof compareShadowProjections = function | typeof projectLegacyImport = function`, NODE_EXIT=0.
Both live function values came back, so Node did not merely locate the package - it EVALUATED packages/import/src/index.ts and produced the real bindings. That is a `.ts` export target (`exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}`) executed on Node v24.16.0 under native type stripping.

NO FLAG, NO PATHS, NO DEEP IMPORT. The command carries no --experimental-*, no --loader, no --import, no tsconfig paths, no relative path. I did not copy the tools/import/import-shadow.ts precedent (`../../packages/import/src/index.js`), which rail 1 forbids here and which would have proven nothing since a deep relative import needs no edge at all. DoD 4 met exactly as written.

CONTROL A - not root hoisting. `Test-Path node_modules/@moe/import` at the repo root -> `False`. There is no hoisted copy for the daemon to walk up to, so the success above had to come through apps/daemon's own resolution.

CONTROL B - nonexistent specifier, same shape, same cwd: `import('@moe/does-not-exist')` from apps/daemon -> `FAILED code= ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, exit 1. So the positive is not a harness that swallows errors.

CONTROL C, the decisive one - the SAME REAL SPECIFIER from a package WITHOUT the edge: `import('@moe/import')` with cwd `packages/store` (which does not declare @moe/import) -> `FAILED code= ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, exit 1. Identical specifier, identical Node, identical command; only the declaring manifest differs. This is what makes the positive attributable to THIS TASK'S manifest+lock edge rather than to anything ambient in the workspace.

Mechanism, for the record: `pnpm install --lockfile-only` in step 3 also materialised the workspace symlink `apps/daemon/node_modules/@moe/import -> /d/projexts/moe-next/packages/import`. That link is the edge at runtime; it exists for apps/daemon and does not exist for packages/store, which is precisely the difference controls B and C isolate.

No file was created or left behind by this step - every probe was an inline `-e` expression, so there is nothing in `git status` to clean up.

THE LOCKFILE IS THE ONLY RISKY FILE HERE. `pnpm install` can rewrite far more than the one importer entry — peer resolutions, formatting, unrelated blocks — and rail 2 requires unrelated changes to be PRESERVED. There is no partial-file commit available here, so a polluted lock is a stop-and-report, not a judgement call.
2. A WSL-stamped `node_modules` makes Windows pnpm fail in ways that read like a manifest error rather than an environment one. Check before concluding the manifest edit was wrong.
3. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL MUST FAIL FOR THE RIGHT REASON. A probe that errors on a syntax mistake, an unused import, or a lint rule satisfies "it failed" while proving nothing about module resolution. Read the actual diagnostic code and require it to be the module-not-found family.
4. THE STEP-1 BASELINE PROBE MUST FAIL. If it passes before the manifest edit, the edge already exists by some route and the task premise is wrong — stop and report rather than landing a no-op edit and claiming the probe as evidence.
